question: After correcting display/registration translation, do real designer red-before and blue-after outlines remain materially different, or is most observed offset a uniform display shift?
training_data: top 50% of cropped overlay; deterministic stride <=3000 points
withheld_data: bottom 50%; optimization prohibited on these pixels
candidate_registration: blue-after -> red-before; horizontal shift -50 to +50 integer px step 2; vertical shift -20 to +20 integer px step 2
optimization: minimize median nearest-before-pixel distance among top 50% blue-after sample (distance transform of red-before)
validate: Report no-alignment vs training-fit alignment on held-out bottom 50% independently, plus percent of after contour points >4 and >10 pixels from nearest before
inference_boundary: Observed offsets in rasterized before/after composite do not reveal designer intent, original B-spline edits, pen motion, or aesthetic superiority
rights: Transient source bytes only; public repository stores derived aggregates and hashes, not photos or contour point coordinates.
stop_conditions: fewer than 100 qualifying colored pixels per training/heldout region
aligned mask difference below epsilon: record as unidentifiable, not as a proven deformation
